gloss: choose, select, prefer; (rarely) test, prove; the chosen; the choicest
summary: To choose: to pick out one from many, as men for battle, stones from a stream or a bull for sacrifice, and to choose a way, preferring one thing to another, as life or death, Yahweh or other gods. Above all Yahweh chooses: Abraham and his seed, Israel to be his treasured people, Levi and Aaron for the priesthood, Saul, David and his son for king, and the place he will choose to put his name, Jerusalem and Zion, which he will choose again. In Isa 48:10 the choosing is a testing, “I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction”, beside “I have refined you”; the Aramaic and Syriac verb is to test and prove, and the Peshitta uses it for proving faith like gold in the fire. From the root come בָּחִיר “chosen one”, Yahweh's servant, Moses, David and Israel; מִבְחָר “the choicest”; and בָּחוּר, spelled as the participle “chosen”, the usual word for a young man in his strength, whose tie to the root's sense is not clear.

words.gloss: choose, select; prefer; (rarely) test, examine; (niphal) be chosen, be preferable
words.summary: About 170 times, almost all in the qal; the niphal is the passive and in Proverbs “to be preferred, choice”. It takes its object with אֶת or, especially when Yahweh chooses, with בְּ. Its opposite is מָאַס “refuse, reject” (Isa 7:15–16; 41:9; Psa 78:67–68). The brief's tokens with no stem are the noun בָּחוּר and the phrase בָּחֳרִי־אָף “in burning of anger” (Exo 11:8; 1Sa 20:34; Isa 7:4; Lam 2:3; 2Ch 25:10), which is חֳרִי of the root חרה with בְּ, filed here by spelling.

stems.gloss: choose, select; (Yahweh) choose a people, man or place; choose a way, prefer; test, examine; (passive participle) chosen, picked

senses.definition: To take one or some from among many, by looking them over: men for a task or a battle, stones, a bull, a stretch of land, one of several things offered.

evidence.note: Moses to Joshua: “בְּחַר־לָנוּ אֲנָשִׁים and go out, fight with Amalek.”
David “וַיִּבְחַר־לוֹ five smooth stones from the brook”.
Elijah to the prophets of Baal: “Choose for yourselves one bull, and prepare it first.”
“Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan”: the land he looked over and saw well watered (Gen 13:10).
“Three things I lay on you: choose one of them, and I will do it to you.”
Moses chose able men out of all Israel and made them heads over the people.
Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty men of valour.
Saul chose three thousand men of Israel.
Ahithophel: “Let me choose twelve thousand men.”
Joab “chose from all the chosen (בְּחוּרֵי) of Israel”.
The poor man “chooses a tree that will not rot” for his idol.
“All that you choose of me, I will do for you.”
The sons of God “took wives for themselves of all that they chose”.

senses.gloss: (Yahweh) choose a people, a tribe, a man
senses.definition: Yahweh's choosing of a people or a man to belong to him and serve him: Abraham and his seed, Israel out of all peoples, the tribe of Levi and the house of Aaron, a king, a servant. The choice rests on his love and his oath, not on the worth of the one chosen.

evidence.note: “You are a holy people to Yahweh your God; בְּךָ בָּחַר Yahweh your God to be a treasured people for himself out of all the peoples.”
“Not because you were more than all peoples did Yahweh set his love on you and choose you … but because Yahweh loved you and kept the oath he swore to your fathers.”
“Yahweh delighted in your fathers to love them, and chose their seed after them, you, out of all peoples.”
“Because he loved your fathers, he chose their seed after them.”
“You are Yahweh the God who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.”
“Blessed is the nation whose God is Yahweh, the people he has chosen for his inheritance.”
“Yah has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel for his treasure.”
“Israel my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen … I said to you, You are my servant, בְּחַרְתִּיךָ וְלֹא מְאַסְתִּיךָ”: chosen, set against rejected.
“You are my witnesses … and my servant whom I have chosen.”
“Because of Yahweh who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, and he has chosen you.”
“In the day I chose Israel and lifted my hand to the seed of the house of Jacob.”
“Yahweh will have compassion on Jacob, וּבָחַר עוֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, and set them in their own land.”
“The two families which Yahweh chose, he has rejected them”: the people's word, answered in Jer 33:25–26.
“The man whom Yahweh chooses, he shall be holy.”
“The man whom I choose, his rod shall sprout.”
Levi: “Yahweh your God has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to minister in the name of Yahweh.”
“Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest?”
“He sent Moses his servant, Aaron whom he had chosen.”
“You shall surely set a king over you whom Yahweh your God chooses; from among your brothers.”
“Do you see him whom Yahweh has chosen, that there is none like him among all the people?”
Of Jesse's sons, one after another: “Yahweh has not chosen this one.”
“Before Yahweh, who chose me above your father.”
“He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds.”
“He refused (וַיִּמְאַס) the tent of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim, but chose the tribe of Judah.”
Yahweh chose Judah, the house of Jesse, David, and of David's sons Solomon, “for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father”.
“David my servant whom I chose.”
“I will take you, Zerubbabel my servant … and make you as a signet, כִּי־בְךָ בָחַרְתִּי.”
“The God of this people Israel chose our fathers”: Paul's summary of Deu 4:37; 7:7.

senses.definition: The place Yahweh chooses “to put his name there”, where Israel is to bring its offerings and keep its feasts; named at last as Jerusalem and Zion, chosen with David, cast off for its sins, and to be chosen again.

evidence.note: “The place which Yahweh your God will choose out of all your tribes to put his name there.”
Three times a year all males appear “in the place which he will choose”.
“I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.”
“But I chose Jerusalem that my name might be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel.”
“Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.”
“The tribe of Judah, mount Zion which he loved.”
“Yahweh has chosen Zion; he has desired (אִוָּהּ) it for his dwelling.”
“I will cast off this city which I have chosen, Jerusalem.”
“From there I will gather them and bring them to the place I have chosen to make my name dwell there.”
“Yahweh will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem.”
“Yahweh will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem.”
“Yahweh rebuke you, adversary; Yahweh who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you.”
Of the house: “I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.”
“He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob whom he loved.”

senses.gloss: choose (a way), prefer, take one's side
senses.definition: Of a man: to choose between two courses, gods or ways, taking one and leaving the other; with מִן, to prefer one thing to another. What a man chooses shows what he delights in.

evidence.note: “Life and death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse; וּבָחַרְתָּ בַּחַיִּים, that you may live, you and your seed.”
“Choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve … but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.”
“You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen Yahweh, to serve him.”
“That he may know to refuse (מָאוֹס) the evil and choose (וּבָחוֹר) the good.”
“Better is a day in your courts than a thousand; בָּחַרְתִּי to stand at the threshold of the house of my God than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.”
“My soul chooses strangling, death rather than my bones.”
“Do not turn to iniquity, for this you have chosen rather than affliction.”
“The way of faithfulness I have chosen.”
“I have chosen your precepts.”
“Who is the man who fears Yahweh? Him he will teach in the way he should choose.”
“They hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of Yahweh.”
“Do not envy a man of violence, and do not choose any of his ways.”
The eunuchs “who keep my sabbaths and choose what I delight in (חָפַצְתִּי) and hold fast my covenant”.
“You did evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I did not delight.”
“They have chosen their own ways … I also will choose their delusions.”
“Is it such a fast that I have chosen? … Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of wickedness?”
“You will be ashamed of the gardens that you have chosen.”
Of the idols: “an abomination is he who chooses you”.
“They chose new gods; then war was in the gates.”
“Go and cry to the gods whom you have chosen.”
“You will cry out because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves.”
Saul to Jonathan: “Do I not know that בֹחֵר אַתָּה לְבֶן־יִשַׁי”: you have sided with the son of Jesse.
“I chose their way and sat as chief.”
“How then should I answer him, choose my words with him?”
“You choose the tongue of the crafty.”
Moses “choosing rather (ἑλόμενος) to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”: the preferring of Psa 84:11.

senses.definition: To try a thing to find its worth, as metal in the furnace, and so to discern what is good. Clear in Isa 48:10, where it stands beside צָרַף “refine”, and in Job 34:4 beside “let us know”.

evidence.note: “Behold, I have refined you (צְרַפְתִּיךָ), but not as silver; בְּחַרְתִּיךָ in the furnace of affliction”: the choosing is a proving in the fire.
“Let us choose (examine) judgment for ourselves; let us know (נֵדְעָה) among ourselves what is good”: the hearers are to test the words, as “the ear tests (תִּבְחָן) words” (Job 34:3).
“For you must choose, and not I”: Job is to judge the matter.

senses.definition: בָּחוּר as the participle: picked men, chosen out for war, and once of excellent cedars. Where it stands with אִישׁ or a number of soldiers it is “chosen”; it is spelled as the noun “young man”.

evidence.note: Pharaoh “took six hundred chosen chariots (רֶכֶב בָּחוּר)”.
“Seven hundred אִישׁ בָּחוּר, left-handed, each slinging a stone at a hair and not missing.”
“Three thousand chosen men out of all Israel.”
“David gathered again all the chosen of Israel, thirty thousand.”
“A hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, makers of war.”
“Three hundred thousand chosen men, able to go out to war, handling spear and shield.”
“His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.”
“I have exalted בָחוּר מֵעָם”: one chosen out of the people, David (Psa 89:21); the same spelling as “young man”.
“Who is chosen, whom I may appoint over her?” (also Jer 50:44).

senses.gloss: be chosen rather than; be preferable, choice
senses.definition: To be the thing chosen over another, and so to be better, more to be desired; as an adjective, “choice” silver. Once of death chosen rather than life.

evidence.note: “A name נִבְחָר rather than great riches, favour better than silver and gold.”
“To get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver.”
“To do righteousness and justice נִבְחָר to Yahweh more than sacrifice.”
“Knowledge rather than choice gold.”
“My produce than choice silver.”
“The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth little.”
“וְנִבְחַר מָוֶת מֵחַיִּים for all the remnant that remain of this evil family.”

evidence.locator: Deu.12.5, יִבְחַר → ἐκλέξηται; Deu.30.19, וּבָחַרְתָּ → ἔκλεξαι; Isa.7.15, וּבָחוֹר → ἐκλέξασθαι; ἐκλέγομαι renders בָּחַר ×101

evidence.note: “The God of this people Israel chose (ἐξελέξατο) our fathers”: Deu 4:37; 7:7.
“For the sake of the chosen, whom he chose (ἐξελέξατο), he has shortened the days.”
“Has not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom?”
Jesus chose twelve of his disciples.

evidence.locator: Jos.24.15, בַּחֲרוּ → ἕλεσθε; Job.34.4, נִבְחֲרָה → ἑλώμεθα

evidence.note: “Choosing rather (μᾶλλον ἑλόμενος) to suffer affliction with the people of God.”
“What I shall choose (αἱρήσομαι) I do not know.”
“God chose (εἵλετο) you from the beginning for salvation.”
Isa 42:1 quoted of Jesus: “Behold my servant whom I have chosen (ὃν ᾑρέτισα)”, for the Hebrew בְּחִירִי.

parallels.note: Yahweh chose because he loved: the fathers, Zion.
To choose is to choose what one delights in.
“Yahweh has chosen Zion; he has desired it for his dwelling.”
Refine: the parallel that shows בָּחַר as testing.

opposites.note: Refuse, reject: what is not chosen.

phrases.gloss: the place which Yahweh will choose (to put his name there)
choose (a person or place), especially of Yahweh's choosing

words.summary: About forty-five times: a young man in his strength, set beside the virgin and against the old man, and the young men of a people as its fighting men. It is spelled as the verb's passive participle “chosen”, and some verses can be read either way (Psa 89:20; 1Sa 9:2, Saul “a בָּחוּר and good”), but how “young man” comes from “choose” is not clear: no cognate yet found shares the meaning, so the root's other cognates count against it.

senses.definition: A grown young man, unmarried or newly married, in the strength of his years: paired with בְּתוּלָה “virgin” and set against זָקֵן “old man”.

evidence.note: “The glory of young men is their strength, and the splendour of old men is grey hair.”
“As a young man marries a virgin, so shall your sons marry you.”
“Young men and virgins, old men with youths.”
“Both young man and virgin, the suckling with the grey-haired man.”
The king of the Chaldeans “slew their young men with the sword … and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or aged”.
“Youths shall faint and be weary, and young men shall utterly stumble; but those who wait on Yahweh shall renew their strength.”
“Rejoice, young man, in your youth … but know that for all these God will bring you into judgment.”
Ruth did not go “after the young men, whether poor or rich”.
Samson made a feast, “for so the young men used to do”.
“Your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions”, quoted at Act 2:17.
“I raised up of your young men for Nazirites.”
“The fair virgins and the young men shall faint for thirst.”
Saul, “a young man and good (בָּחוּר וָטוֹב)”: perhaps “choice and good”.
The king “will take your choicest young men”.
“Desirable young men, all of them, horsemen riding on horses.”

senses.gloss: young men (as a people's fighting men)
senses.definition: The young men of a city or nation as the ones who go to war and fall by the sword in its judgment.

evidence.note: “Let their young men be slain by the sword in battle.”
Assyria: “his young men shall become forced labour”.
“Her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be cut off.”
“The choicest of his young men (מִבְחַר בַּחוּרָיו) have gone down to the slaughter.”
“Your young men I slew with the sword.”
“He has called an assembly against me to crush my young men.”
“He struck down the young men of Israel.”

evidence.locator: Jol.3.1, בַּחוּרֵיכֶם → νεανίσκοι; Isa.40.30 → νεανίσκοι; Ecc.11.9 → νεανίσκε; νεανίσκος renders בָּחוּר ×17

evidence.note: Jol 3:1 quoted at Pentecost: “your young men (οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν) shall see visions”.
“I have written to you, young men, because you are strong”: the strength of Pro 20:29.

parallels.note: Virgin: the young man's fixed partner, “young man and virgin”.

opposites.note: The old man: strength set against grey hair.

phrases.gloss: young man and virgin: the whole of a people's youth

words.summary: Fourteen times, always in the construct before what it picks out: the choicest of tombs, cedars, valleys, a flock, men. Twice spelled מִבְחוֹר (2Ki 3:19; 19:23), which BDB also files as b.bg.ah; the tokens are counted here once.

senses.definition: What would be chosen out of a class as the best of it.

evidence.note: “In the choicest of our tombs bury your dead.”
“Take the choicest of the flock.”
“All your choice vows which you vow to Yahweh.”
“His chosen officers are sunk in the Sea of Reeds.”
“They shall cut down your choicest cedars.”
“Its choicest cypresses” (מִבְחוֹר; also Isa 37:24, מִבְחַר).
“Every fortified city and every choice city” (מִבְחוֹר).
“Your choicest valleys were full of chariots.”
“The choicest of his young men have gone down to the slaughter.”
“The choicest of the sons of Assyria, all of them.”
“The choice and best of Lebanon.”
“His chosen people (עַם מִבְחָרָיו)”: picked troops, who have no strength to stand.

words.summary: Thirteen times, always of Yahweh's chosen, nearly always with “my”, “his” or “your”: Israel and Jacob, Moses, David, the servant of Isa 42. The New Testament's “the elect” (ἐκλεκτός) is its Greek.

senses.definition: One whom Yahweh has chosen for himself: the people of Israel as a whole, or a man chosen to serve him.

evidence.note: “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; בְּחִירִי, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him.” Quoted of Jesus at Mat 12:18.
“I have made a covenant with my chosen; I have sworn to David my servant.”
“Had not Moses his chosen one stood in the breach before him.”
“Seed of Abraham his servant, sons of Jacob his chosen ones” (also 1Ch 16:13).
“He brought out … his chosen ones with singing, and gave them the lands of the nations.”
“That I may see the good of your chosen ones.”
“To give drink to my people, my chosen”, taken up at 1Pe 2:9.
“You are a chosen race (γένος ἐκλεκτόν) … a people for his own possession”: Isa 43:20–21 with Exo 19:5–6.
“For the sake of Jacob my servant and Israel my chosen.”
“My chosen ones shall inherit it (my mountains), and my servants shall dwell there.”
“You shall leave your name for a curse to my chosen.”
“My chosen ones shall long enjoy the work of their hands.”
The Gibeonites: “in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Yahweh”.

evidence.locator: Isa.42.1, בְּחִירִי → ἐκλεκτός; Psa.89.4 → ἐκλεκτοῖς; Psa.105.6 → ἐκλεκτοί; Isa.43.20 → τὸ ἐκλεκτόν; ἐκλεκτός renders בָּחִיר ×9

evidence.note: “A chosen race”, the Septuagint of Isa 43:20 “τὸ γένος μου τὸ ἐκλεκτόν”.
The rulers mock: “if this is the Christ, the chosen of God (ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκλεκτός)”, the title of Isa 42:1.
Jesus the living stone, “rejected by men, but chosen (ἐκλεκτόν) by God, precious”.
“They shall gather his elect from the four winds.”
“Who shall bring any charge against God's elect?”
“Those with him are called and chosen and faithful.”

words.summary: An abstract plural, three times, the time of life of the בָּחוּר; it shares that word's uncertain tie to the root.

senses.gloss: youth, the days of young manhood
senses.definition: The years of a man's youth and strength.

evidence.note: “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth (בְּחוּרֹתֶיךָ), before the evil days come.”
“Rejoice, young man (בָּחוּר) in your youth … in the days of your young manhood.”
“Joshua the son of Nun, minister of Moses from his youth (מִבְּחֻרָיו).”

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb, nine times: to look closely at and discern, and in the passive to be tried and proved, as gold in the fire. It is the sense of the Hebrew in Isa 48:10 and Job 34:4; the Peshitta's word for “choose” is another root (ܓܒܐ).

senses.definition: To examine with the eyes and so perceive what is there.

evidence.note: “The beam that is in your own eye לָא בָּחַר אַנְתְּ”: you do not consider.
Isa 6:9 quoted: “seeing you shall see and not perceive (לָא תֵּבְחֲרוּן)”, for the Hebrew “and do not know (תֵּדָעוּ)”.
“Eyes that they should not perceive (נֵבְחֲרוּן) with them.”

senses.definition: Of gold: proved in the fire.

evidence.note: “Buy from me gold דַּבְחִיר מֵן נוּרָא”: tried from the fire.

senses.definition: To be tried by trial or fire and found true.

evidence.note: “Blessed is the man who endures trials, for when he has been proved (דֶּאתְבְּחַר) he will receive the crown of life.”
“The heavens, being tried (מֵתְבַּחְרִין) in fire, shall be loosed.”
“Then it will be clear to you (נֵתְבְּחַר לָךְ) to cast out the splinter”: you will see plainly.

words.summary: The Peshitta's noun from the verb, three times, all in 1 Peter.

senses.definition: The testing that shows what a thing is worth, as gold in the fire; and the day of God's scrutiny.

evidence.note: “That the proving (בּוּחְרָנָא) of your faith may be found more precious than refined gold tried in the fire.”
“Do not be amazed at the trial that comes upon you, as though a strange thing happened to you, for it is for your proving.”
“That they may glorify God in the day of scrutiny (בְּיוֹמָא דְּבוּחְרָנָא)”, for the Greek ἐπισκοπῆς.

words.summary: Once in the Peshitta, of the stone of Isa 28:16, where the Hebrew has אֶבֶן בֹּחַן “a tested stone” and the Greek ἐκλεκτόν “chosen”: the Syriac word holds both.

senses.definition: Proved and found good, and so chosen.

evidence.note: Isa 28:16 quoted: “Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, בְּחִירְתָּא and precious, at the head of the corner.”
The Hebrew: “a stone, a tested stone (אֶבֶן בֹּחַן), a precious corner of a sure foundation.”

cognates.note: Choosing and examining in one verb, as the Hebrew has both; the adjective is the “choice” of מִבְחָר and the niphal. Akkadian lost ḥ (and ʿ) with an e-colouring of the vowel, as in bêru, but kept ḫ; so the word shows ḥ behind ח.

evidence.note: Meanings in the glossaries: choose, choosing, examine, put aside?, select; written forms abīar, ibtēru, libēru, nibtīar.
choice; selected.

cognates.gloss: try, test; choose, select; (aphel) pick out; (בְּחִיר) chosen, select; tried, purified
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums: both sides of the Hebrew. The Targum of Jer 17:10 uses it for the Hebrew בֹּחֵן “I test the heart”, and of Psa 33:12 for “the people he has chosen”; בְּחִיר renders “the chosen of Yahweh” (2Sa 21:6) and “his chosen ones” (Psa 105:6), and “tried” of the word of Yahweh (Psa 18:31).

evidence.locator: s.v. בְּחַר (ch.), citing Targ. Jer. XVII, 10 (try, test; h. text בחן); Targ. Ps. XXXIII, 12 (choose); Y. Sabb. VII, 10a (Af. pick out)
s.v. בְּחִיר (ch.), citing Targ. II Sam. XXI, 6; Targ. Ps. CV, 6 (chosen, select); Targ. Ps. XVIII, 31 (tried, purified)

doctrine.statement: Yahweh chose Abram, brought him out of Ur, and covenanted to give the land to his seed (Neh 9:7–8). He chose Israel “to be a treasured people for himself out of all the peoples”, not because they were many, “but because Yahweh loved you and kept the oath he swore to your fathers” (Deu 7:6–8; 10:15; 4:37). He brought out “his chosen ones” and gave them the lands of the nations (Psa 105:43–44). When the people said Yahweh had rejected the two families he chose, he answered that he would no more reject the seed of Jacob and David than his covenant with day and night, “for I will return their captivity and have compassion on them” (Jer 33:24–26); “I have chosen you and not rejected you” (Isa 41:9). He “will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, and the stranger will join himself to them” (Isa 14:1); “my chosen ones shall inherit it (my mountains), and my servants shall dwell there” (Isa 65:9), while those who chose what he did not delight in leave their name for a curse to his chosen (Isa 65:12, 15). Paul says of Israel, “as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers' sake; for the gifts and calling of God are without repentance” (Rom 11:28–29). From the verses: the choice rests on Yahweh's love and his oath to the fathers, not on Israel's worth; it is not undone by their scattering; and it is tied to the land promised to Abraham, which the chosen will yet inherit when Yahweh chooses Israel again and settles them there, with the nations joined to them.

Israel was to bring its offerings and keep its feasts “in the place which Yahweh your God will choose out of all your tribes to put his name there” (Deu 12:5; 16:16). Solomon heard Yahweh say, “I chose no city … but I chose Jerusalem that my name might be there, and I chose David to be over my people Israel” (2Ch 6:5–6); “Yahweh has chosen Zion; he has desired it for his dwelling: this is my resting place for ever; here I will dwell” (Psa 132:13–14). For Judah's sins he said, “I will cast off this city which I have chosen” (2Ki 23:27), yet the prophets after the exile say, “Yahweh will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem” (Zec 1:17), “Yahweh will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem” (Zec 2:16). Jesus called Jerusalem “the city of the great King” (Mat 5:35), and the angel promised that God would give him “the throne of his father David” (Luk 1:32). From the verses: Jerusalem was chosen together with David's house; its casting off was for a time; and Yahweh will choose it again as the seat of David's throne when the son of David reigns there.

Yahweh says, “Behold my servant, whom I uphold; my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him” (Isa 42:1), and Matthew applies the words to Jesus (Mat 12:17–18). Of David, “I have exalted one chosen out of the people; I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him … he shall cry to me, You are my Father” (Psa 89:20–21, 27), and the covenant is “with my chosen … to David my servant” (Psa 89:4). At the cross the rulers mocked him as “the Christ, the chosen of God” (Luk 23:35); Peter calls him the stone “rejected by men, but chosen by God” (1Pe 2:4). The child of Isa 7:14, applied to Jesus at Mat 1:23, would grow “that he may know to refuse the evil and choose the good” (Isa 7:15), and he was “in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (Heb 4:15). From the verses: the chosen one is a man taken “out of the people”, chosen and upheld by Yahweh, given Yahweh's spirit, and calling Yahweh his Father: the chosen of God, not God himself. His choosing of the good was a real choice, made in our nature under temptation.

Moses set before Israel “life and good, death and evil … therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your seed, to love Yahweh your God, to obey his voice and to cleave to him, for he is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land” (Deu 30:15, 19–20). Joshua said, “choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve” (Jos 24:15). Those who “did not choose the fear of Yahweh” eat the fruit of their own way (Pro 1:29–31), and of a rebellious remnant Jeremiah says, “death shall be chosen rather than life” (Jer 8:3). From the verses: life is not something a man has in himself; it is set before him by Yahweh, who “is your life”, and it is had by choosing to love and obey him; the other choice is death.

NAMES: יִבְחָר Ibhar (b.bg.af, with the zero-token cross-reference j.ag.ad) is in names/ibhar.json; מִבְחָר Mibhar (b.bg.ai) is in names/mibhar.json. LEFT OUT: the place בַּחֻרִים Bahurim (b.bg.ae; TIPNR Bahurim@2Sa.3.16 is a place) and the gentilic בַּחֲרוּמִי Baharumite (b.bg.aj, 1Ch 11:33; Barhumite at 2Sa 23:31, see names/azmaveth.json): places have no name entries and their keys are not claimed. b.bg.ah (מִבְחוֹר, 2Ki 3:19; 19:23) lists the same tokens as b.bg.ag and is not named; m.ai.am, its zero-token cross-reference, is put on מִבְחָר. The brief's verb tokens with no stem include בָּחֳרִי־אַף (Exo 11:8; 1Sa 20:34; Isa 7:4; Lam 2:3; 2Ch 25:10), which is חֳרִי (root חרה) with בְּ, filed here by spelling, and the noun בָּחוּר. PUAL: Ecc 9:4 ketiv יְבֻחַר, qere יְחֻבַּר (חבר), not entered; the text read follows the qere. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) בָּחוּר “young man”: no cognate shares the meaning, and the link to “choose” is not shown. The verses where “chosen” and “young man” meet (1Sa 9:2; Psa 89:20; Jer 48:15 מִבְחַר בַּחוּרָיו; the picked men of war) could support “young men as the choice, fighting men”, but this is not argued in the entry. A lead: Neo-Assyrian bahūlātu “men, troops” (Oracc armep x000086970) has l for r and h (= ḫ) and is not a regular correspondence; not recorded. (2) The “test” sense rests on Isa 48:10 and Job 34:4 with the Aramaic and Syriac; 1QIsaᵃ reads בחנתיכה at Isa 48:10, and Hebrew בחן “test” is near in sound and sense; whether בחר “test” is a separate older root or the same choosing-by-examination is not decided (Akkadian bêru has both “choose” and “examine”, which argues one root). NOT RECORDED: Ge'ez ኀረየ ḫarya “choose” (Wiktionary links it to בָּחַר) has a different root ḫ-r-y and is not a cognate; Arabic بحر (Lane, “slit; sea”) does not share the meaning; a Bedouin Arabic baḥara “look around” is a lead from another lexicon, not followed to a dictionary. No Ugaritic or Phoenician form checked. The Peshitta's NT words are from SEDRA root 259 BKR (lexemes 366 BKR, 365 BOKRNA, 114 BK;RA); its word for “choose” is ܓܒܐ, and its Mat 12:18 has ܐܨܛܒܝܬ, so no Peshitta link to Isa 42:1's בְּחִירִי.
